lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Plan a two-beat scene where a character wants the last seat on a bus. Include one clear reaction.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Beat 1: race for the seat. Beat 2: see an elderly passenger—character gives up the seat. Reaction shows values.'

WATCH FOR
Writing long speeches with no reaction. Drama needs change between beats.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Write and perform a one-minute two-character scene with circumstances, two beats and a visible reaction. Reflect on what your body showed.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: Circumstances: lost property room after lunch. Beat 1: two students search. Beat 2: one finds a diary and hesitates. Reaction: the owner enters and both freeze, then negotiate kindly.

TRY FIRST
Plan a two-beat scene where a character wants the last seat on a bus. Include one clear reaction.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Beat 1: race for the seat. Beat 2: see an elderly passenger—character gives up the seat. Reaction shows values.'
teach_steps.explain:
A character scene has given circumstances (who, where, when) and beats (small units where the action shifts). Strong scenes show reactions: characters change because of what they hear. Keep dialogue short and playable; show more than you tell.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the elements, techniques or performance choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For movement or instruments, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby and stop if anything feels unsafe. You may always describe a choice instead of performing it. One deliberate artistic choice with a named effect is more useful than a longer praise sentence.
teach_steps.notice: Writing long speeches with no reaction. Drama needs change between beats. Name the element or technique and its effect, not just decoration.
